related_resources.reason: Local Picard–Lindelöf theorem and contraction via Picard iteration.
Direction fields, existence and uniqueness, Euler integration, phase lines and stability.

authorship.scope: New standalone foundation-first lecture and mathematical companion; earlier manuscripts retained.

prerequisites.reason: Interpret a first-order initial-value problem and a solution interval.
Recognize that a candidate solution requires verification and a domain.

recommended.reason: Optional review of derivatives as local rates before solving differential equations.

background: Single-variable derivatives, functions and graphs, exponentials, and elementary algebra; lecture 050000 also uses sine and cosine. No PDE prerequisites.
readiness_checks: Exhibit two distinct solutions of a continuous, non-Lipschitz ODE with the same initial state.
Carry out two Picard iterates for a scalar IVP.
State the hypotheses and limitations of a finite-time Gronwall bound.

description: Distinguishes existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence of initial-value solutions, using examples where continuity does not imply uniqueness.
